newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Supreme Court clears Enron project.
newsitem.headline: India's Supreme Court clears Enron project.

text.p: India's Supreme Court on Friday rejected a legal complaint seeking to halt a $2.3 billion power project being built by a subsidiary of U.S.-based Enron Corp.

But the court issued notice to the government of the western state of Maharashtra, which had scrapped and then later approved India's biggest single foreign investment, to explain the shift in its stance.
"At this stage it is not in public interest to re-examine the validity of the power project and the related contract," a three-judge bench said.
"We do not consider in public interest reopening of the Enron contract and therefore we are not expressing any opinion on this issue."
But the court agreed to examine a plea alleging inconsistency on the part of the Maharashtra government. The narrower plea was not expected to call into question the project, lawyers said.
The court was responding to a legal petition filed by the Centre for Indian Trade Union, which challenged the project's approval by the Central Electricity Authority.
The trade union body had appealed to the Supreme Court after the Bombay High Court dismissed a lawsuit against the Dabhol Power Company, an Enron unit, in December.
Work on the 2,450-megawatt power plant resumed late last year after the ruling Hindu nationalist government renegotiated a contract it had claimed was too expensive.
The court set a hearing on the matter of shifts in the Maharashtra government's stance for July 14.
